SK7082 The conditional expressions are nested

Conditional expressions nest more deeply than dotnet_code_quality.SK7082.threshold (default 1), counting a right-associated ladder as one level.

CategoryMaintainability
Default severitysuggestion
ScopeSyntax
Needs a compilationno
Runs under --load=looseyes
Cached per fileyes
Fixno
Language version floor—
Since1.3
SupersedesS3358

Why

Nested ?: is the one expression form where operator precedence and reader expectation reliably disagree: a ? b : c ? d : e groups one way and a ? b ? c : d : e another, and neither grouping is visible without counting. ⚠ The measurement makes one distinction that decides whether the rule is usable at all: a right-associated ladder — a ? x : b ? y : z — costs one level, not one per rung. That shape is an else if chain written as an expression; it reads top to bottom, each condition is tested once, and charging it per rung would make the rule fire on the one nested form that is idiomatic. What costs a level is a ?: anywhere else inside another: in the condition, in the true branch, or buried inside the false branch rather than being it. Rewriting a nest is a judgement about which branch deserves a name, so there is no fix.

Example

Instead of:

var label = ready ? (loud ? "READY" : "ready") : "waiting";

Write:

var word = loud ? "READY" : "ready";
var label = ready ? word : "waiting";

// and the ladder, which is one level and never reported:
var size = n < 10 ? "small" : n < 100 ? "medium" : "large";

When it does not fire

A metric rule has no false positives in the sense doc 16 § R3 means: it reports a measurement against a threshold, and the measurement is either right or a bug. ⚠ The right-associated ladder is exempt and that exemption is the rule. Without it the default threshold would fire on n < 10 ? "small" : n < 100 ? "medium" : "large", which no reader has ever had trouble with, and the category would be switched off within a day. Parentheses around a ladder rung do not change the number, because some house styles write them and some do not. ⚠ A lambda body restarts the count, exactly as SK7006's nesting depth does: xs.Select(x => x > 0 ? a : b) written inside a conditional is not a nested conditional in any sense a reader experiences. ⚠ An interpolation hole restarts it too, and for the rule's own reason. The rule exists because precedence and reader expectation disagree about ?:; inside $"…{…}…" they cannot, because the hole has explicit delimiters and C# requires a conditional written in one to be parenthesised — a bare : there is the format specifier. There is nothing left to mis-group. ⚠ Only the outermost conditional of a nest reports — every conditional in the compilation reaches the analyzer, and reporting each would produce one finding per level pointing at the same expression, with the innermost carrying the smallest number. A null-conditional ?. and a null-coalescing ?? are different operators and are not counted. Generated code is excluded. The finding points at the outermost ? token.

Configuration

  • dotnet_code_quality.SK7082.threshold
  • dotnet_diagnostic.SK7082.severity
